data.title: Anthropic's Amodei And Nvidia's Huang Clash Over AI Safety At Salesforce Dreamforce
data.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang offered contrasting views on artificial intelligence safety at Salesforce's Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where Salesforce also announced a new reasoning model for its Agentforce platform built on one of Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron models. Amodei, speaking with Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, said the industry should set an example and slow the pace of model development, while Huang argued that market forces already provide discipline and that speed and safety can coexist. Benioff said companies should slow down or speed up as they see fit, but should be held accountable. Salesforce and Anthropic also expanded their strategic partnership late last month and unveiled Claudeforce, a new way for salespeople to access data directly inside Anthropic's Claude chatbot.

data.title: Bitcoin Falls 4% as Senate Blocks Clarity Act
data.description:
The Senate blocked the Clarity Act after the bill received 49 votes for and 50 against, falling short of the 60 votes needed to advance. According to NS3.AI, the proposal would divide oversight of digital assets among regulators and classify them as securities, commodities or stablecoins.

Bitcoin traded at $75,997 after falling 4% in 24 hours. U.S. President Donald Trump urged lawmakers to pass the bill last month.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff on AI Safety: Enterprises and Tech Executives Must Be Held Accountable
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Salesforce Chief Executive Officer Marc Benioff said at a Salesforce event that enterprises and technology executives must be held accountable for the technology they develop.

data.title: STOCKS | JPMorgan Expects Third-Quarter Growth in Trading and Investment Banking Fees
data.description:
JPMorgan expects third-quarter trading revenue and investment banking fee income to grow, contrasting with a warning from Bank of America on Monday. According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan Co-President Doug Petno said at a Barclays conference on Tuesday that trading revenue for the quarter ended September 30 is expected to rise about 15% to 19% year over year, and that investment banking fee income is also expected to post a similar increase.

Petno's remarks came as Bank of America said on Monday that its third-quarter trading revenue was expected to be relatively flat year over year. After Petno spoke, JPMorgan shares briefly rose 0.9%, reversing earlier losses.

data.title: STOCKS | S&P 500 Falls 0.4% as Energy Gains 2%
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the S&P 500 Index initially fell 0.4%, with consumer discretionary down 2%, telecom down 0.8%, technology down 0.4%, and energy up 2%; the Nasdaq 100 initially fell 0.7%, with AXON down 9.7%, Strategy down 5.6%, ALNY down 5%, TTWO, Seagate Technology, Western Digital, Synopsys, MercadoLibre, HONA, and SpaceX each down at least 3%, while Marvell Technology rose 1.2%, AMD rose 2.1%, Diamondback Energy rose 2.7%, CrowdStrike rose 2.9%, and Qualcomm rose 4.2%; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 0.3%, while the memory chip index fell 1.4%.

data.title: OranjeBTC Launches Bitcoin-Backed Digital Credit ETF on Brazil's B3
data.description: BitcoinTreasuries.NET said on X that OranjeBTC (OBTC3) has launched DIGY11, described as the world’s first Bitcoin-backed digital credit thematic ETF, on B3, Brazil’s largest stock exchange. According to Odaily, the ETF targets an annualized return of about 18% and pays monthly.

data.title: STOCKS | ICE Sugar and Coffee Futures Fall in New York Late Trading
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, ICE raw sugar futures fell 0.99% and ICE white sugar futures fell 0.64% in late New York trading on Tuesday, September 15, while ICE Arabica coffee futures fell 0.76%, coffee "C" futures fell 2.46%, Robusta coffee futures fell 1.70%, New York cocoa futures fell 2.71% to $5,860 per ton, London cocoa futures fell 0.12%, Chicago WCE canola futures rose 0.72%, and ICE cotton futures fell 0.06%.

data.title: Senate Democrats Block Crypto Regulatory Framework Bill in 49-50 Vote
data.description: Senate Democrats blocked legislation to create a cryptocurrency regulatory framework in a 49-50 vote. According to NS3.AI, Democrats pushed for stronger ethics restrictions on U.S. President Donald Trump's crypto investments while the bill sought to establish uniform rules for the $2.3 trillion cryptocurrency market. The measure had backing from the industry but failed to advance in the Senate.

data.title: Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close Venue Immediately for Renovation
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the Kennedy Center board voted on the 15th to immediately close the center for renovation after U.S. District Court Judge Christopher Cooper rejected the board's proposal to add U.S. President Donald Trump's name again to the building's exterior wall.

data.title: Bitcoin Leads Broad Digital Asset Retreat After U.S. Senate Fails to Pass Crypto Regulatory Bill
data.description: Bitcoin led a broad retreat in digital assets Tuesday after a wide-reaching crypto regulatory bill failed to pass the US Senate. According to Bloomberg, the setback removed one of the industry’s few potential catalysts as anxiety in markets grew over rising interest rates.

data.title: U.S. Senators Kennedy and Cruz Comment on Failed Clarity Act Vote
data.description:
U.S. Senator John Kennedy said he was not surprised that the Clarity Act failed to pass, but he does not believe the bill is dead. According to Odaily, Kennedy said Democratic colleagues understand the need for a deliberately designed crypto market structure, but the work will have to wait until the lame-duck session.

U.S. Senator Ted Cruz said there is a difference between a bill being "dead" and "almost dead," and he hopes the measure can be revived. Cruz blamed Democrats for the failed vote, saying they were "playing politics" and pushing crypto industry activity and jobs overseas.

data.title: Richards Says It Will Be Hard for the FOMC to Skip a Rate Hike
data.description:
Bond traders are pricing in a Federal Reserve rate increase on Wednesday, with interest-rate swaps tied to the meeting showing more than a 90% chance of a quarter-point move from the current 3.5%-3.75% range, according to Bloomberg.

Kitty Richards, a senior fellow at the Groundwork Collaborative, said on Balance of Power that it will be extremely difficult for the FOMC not to raise rates.

data.title: Sui Says Hashi Mainnet Will Soon Launch to Bring Financial Services to Bitcoin on Sui
data.description: Sui said on X that more than $1.5 trillion worth of Bitcoin is sitting idle because using Bitcoin usually means handing it over to someone else. According to Odaily, Hashi will change that by keeping Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network while opening financial services on Sui, and its mainnet will launch soon.

data.title: AI | Anthropic, Salesforce CEOs Say Firms Need More Help Using AI
data.description: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and Salesforce Inc. Chief Executive Officer Marc Benioff said companies have only just begun using artificial intelligence tools and need more help to get the most benefit for their businesses, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | CFTC Opens Broad Probe Into Voluntary Carbon Credit Market
data.description:
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is conducting a broad probe into the voluntary carbon credit market as scrutiny of the industry grows, according to Bloomberg.

The market expanded after corporations began pledging to cut emissions, but it has since shrunk amid quality concerns and a broader corporate pullback from climate goals.

data.title: Wells Fargo Gains On Slightly Better-Than-Expected Net Interest Margin; Eli Lilly Gets Berenberg Upgrade
data.description: According to CNBC, Wells Fargo shares rose after Chief Financial Officer Michal Santomassimo said at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference that the bank's quarter-to-date net interest margin is roughly flat to 1 basis point lower than its 2.43% level in the second quarter, better than the 3 to 4 basis point decline management had expected. Eli Lilly was upgraded to buy from hold by Berenberg, which said the market is underestimating the drugmaker's acquisition spree and the potential of new pipeline assets. Berenberg said Lilly has committed about $60 billion to more than 25 business development deals so far in 2026, including the $2.8 billion upfront purchase of AtaiBeckley and the Centessa takeover, which carried $6.3 billion upfront and could include another $1.5 billion if regulatory milestones are met.

data.title: Iranian President Pezeshkian Slams Western "Human Rights" Double Standards
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at an event in Tehran on September 14 that the West was disguising itself as a "human rights defender," questioned whether cutting off water and food and bombing civilians could be called counterterrorism, and said Iran would never bow to power.

data.title: Musk Says Starlink V3 Deployment Will Begin This Month
data.description: Elon Musk said Starlink V3 constellation deployment will begin this month, with eventual bandwidth expected to exceed that of the current 11,000-satellite constellation by more than 100 times. According to ChainCatcher, Musk said the upgraded network is intended to deliver a much larger total bandwidth than the existing system.

data.title: BNB Surpasses 720 USDT with a Narrowed 0.71% Decrease in 24 Hours
data.description: On Sep 15, 2026, 19:05 PM(UTC). According to Binance Market Data, BNB has crossed the 720 USDT benchmark and is now trading at 720.809998 USDT, with a narrowed narrowed 0.71% decrease in 24 hours.

data.title: STOCKS | Starbucks Snoopy Cup Resells for Up to 5 Times Retail on StockX
data.description: Starbucks Corp.'s Snoopy glass cup is reselling for as much as five times its retail price on StockX, according to Bloomberg. The merchandise is the latest example of Starbucks using exclusive products to draw customers into its stores.
